use: A UI ticket names its frames and cites these ids. The reviewer answers pass or fail for each cited fact. A group applies to every frame that lists it.

checks.drawn: the page holds it: words, order, parts
checks.style: computed style: font, colour, size, shape
checks.rule: behaviour or data, held by a test

facts.text: Archivo for prose, headings and controls. JetBrains Mono for ids, commands, numbers and status lines.
The background is soft dots under a tint and a sheen. There are no constellation lines.
Orange marks three things only: what spends, what waits on the owner, and a live lease.
Lanes, roles and phase kinds differ by shape and fill, never by a colour of their own.
Every number and name is read from a record. A missing value shows as a placeholder, never a guess.
At phone width menus stack, toolbars wrap, wide tables scroll in their own box, and the page never scrolls sideways.
Every control has a visible name or an accessible one, and a target of at least 44 px.
It is one component, with states idle, working, needs, paused, done and off, plus a listening layer.
Idle hangs plumb, dimmed and still, with room between its circles.
Working swings at full length with a short trail, and large marks never swing in step.
Needs you is frozen bent, never straight, and its last circle is an open orange ring.
From working to needs you it freezes within 2 seconds.
Paused hangs while a ring around the last circle fills as the window resets.
Done is three overlapping circles in the palette green, with no arms.
No signal is outlines and dotted arms with no motion.
The last circle is filled orange only while a lease is live. With needs you, a live lease is a dot inside the ring.
All circles are one size and both arms are one thickness.
Arms, circles and the done green come from the palette. The orange never changes.
With reduced motion each state shows one still pose.
Its state follows the table in frame 65b.

STRIP.applies: The strip, on every tab without an open thread or dock

facts.text: It is one component at the bottom of the tab: the mark in its well, the access line, the waiting chip, a message field, the running count and Stop.
The access line reads the state word, what it is about, and whether a lease is live, then the acts Marimba never takes: land, publish, attest, grant.
The waiting chip counts only items the owner has not set aside, and opens the queue.
Stop is enabled only while something runs, and it needs no signature.
The slash key moves to the message field, and Esc leaves it.
A screen whose column already holds a large mark shows the strip without the well.
The mark hangs from the top bar in the empty margin, with its state word and one line. Below 1,260 px it becomes a small mark in the header.
The owner’s messages are bubbles. Marimba’s replies are plain text with no bubble.
The header has the name, one status line and three icons: runs, driver checks, routes.
A composer sits at the bottom, and the strip is not drawn.
The mark hangs at the head of the dock beside the name, where it was summoned, and the state word.
The access line follows: what it did, what it may do, what it never does.
An about chip names the context and can be removed.
The dock ends with a message field, Queue or Steer, the running count and Stop.
The dock changes what the owner sees, never what the factory did. A change of view has Undo.

The rail lists, in order: Look and feel, Bars, Keys. At a glance, Context, Sources, Routes, Prompt, Steps, Step lines, Harness, Jobs. Blocks, Locked room. Owner presses, Routines, Leases, Factory config.
The rail has four groups, and each says who may change it.
The current page is marked, and each row shows its key.

RUN.applies: A run, its phases and its evidence

facts.text: The header names the run, its state, its workflow, its tier and who drove it.
The first tab is the one its phase kind opens on, as frame 59 says.
Times, counts and identities come from the journal, and an estimate is marked as one.
Lanes keep the dashboard’s own icons.

PRESS.applies: An act only the owner takes

facts.text: The button carries a key glyph, and the exact command it signs is on the card.
Marimba prepares it and never runs it. No agent schema holds the act.
If anything moved while the prompt was open, the press is refused.
Until the passkey path is proven, the same act is a line to copy.
The title invites: tell the factory.
Two cards at most offer where the owner left, each with its state and its spend.
Nothing is sent or started until the owner writes.
The mark is idle and says nothing runs on this thread.
One card holds the whole run: request, route, gates and spend.
The line above the answer says what Marimba read, as step names.
Edit request and Change route are free. Confirm and run is the only orange button.
Nothing starts before the press, and the card covers new, start and run.
The spend line shows calls against the ceiling and the time the gates take.
The card shows diff stat, verdict, journey and candidate.
The legal next acts are listed as command lines with a press: land, journey, rework.
Only steps the host allows appear, read from awsf next.
Open the preview is offered before any press.
Land is refused until the journey is attested on the exact candidate.
The refused turn is shown as one line that names the rule, and says nothing ran.
The blocked card names the gate, the exit code and who named it.
Marimba advises against a plain retry, with a cheaper and a surer way.
The owner may override the advice on the terms shown, and the journal records it.
Continue in a new run is the orange fork. Rework and Cancel are lines below it.
Filters are Open, Landed, All.
One run is promoted with its waterfall and figures. The rest degrade in size and contrast by age.
A blocked run shows the gate and the host’s cause.
A run driven in a direct session is listed and marked as an exception.
Five checks, K1 to K5, each with its own card and its evidence.
K2 lists who may take each legal step.
K4 shows that Marimba ran no owner act.
Doctor sits below and is read only.
None of the checks can be switched off from here.
It says which machine answers, and that the report comes from inside the VM.
Proof on this host lists the full suite, the trap suite and a real run landed from here.
A row that was not measured says so.
Four layers in order, L1 to L4, each with what it does and what it costs.

L3 shows the model and the local one under A/B, as two bars told apart without colour.
The policy table gives builder, reviewer and reason for each task class.
A change is a diff the owner commits.

Each act has Confirm and Flag.
The next lease states scope, may do, never, and when it ends.
No lease is granted for a live night until the trap suite refuses every known trap.
A lease never grants itself, lands, publishes or attests.

Training records are counted by provenance, with zero holding frontier output.
The A/B table shows both models and the change, with no winner coloured.
Promotion is a diff to commit.
The A/B continues after promotion.
Eight categories with a score and its evidence.
Each recommendation becomes a backlog item only on accept.
It reads a project and never writes it.
A four step line: landed, built twice, published to staging, production.
Production waits for the owner and is the only orange step.
Both builds must match before staging.
The factory has no path to production.
Each signal shows its source, its text and the item it became.
A handoff from another project is one row, marked to confirm.
Signals are pulled when the owner opens the panel or when outside CI pushes them.
Nothing watches while the owner is away.
The mark listens: a ring of ticks follows the voice. There is no orb.
The words appear as they are recognised, in the language spoken.
What was heard becomes the same card as the panel.
Speech stays on the Mac.
Nothing runs until the card is confirmed.
The mark hangs from the top of the phone.
The stop, its cause and one way forward are on one screen.
Until the passkey test passes, an owner act is signed on the laptop, and the screen says so.
The strip sits under an unchanged Sessions tab.
The mark rises above the strip in its well.

The tab stays beside the dock, filtered by the answer, with a chip that shows the filter.
The steps Marimba took fold into one line written by a template.

Undo restores the tab’s own view.
The answer lists what changed and what was not touched.
Undo all and Open Bars are offered.
Marimba may change what is under Yours and Marimba’s, and nothing under Only you.
Each change is checked after it is made.
Three kinds of button: view, driver, owner. The kind comes from who may take the step.
The waiting card shows what it signs, the candidate and what it is bound to.

An owner route without a valid signature is refused.
Presses arrive in the order the page states.

A recipe is sketched inside the conversation as it will look.

Why now shows the four measures and their bars.
The tuning card is an ordinary run card.
Retire says what goes, what stays and what is kept, and that nothing is deleted.
Carries over, stays behind, asks again and fits are stated.
Data, pins and permissions do not travel. The recipe does.
Context, Routes, Prompt and Steps each have one card with a way to open it.
The context bar shows held now, when Marimba offers to compact and when a turn waits.
Values are the live ones.
Seven palettes, each drawn with its own colours and its own mark.
Mode is Dark, Light or System.
The pendulum can be stilled.
The last change is named with Undo.
A palette change crosses the mark to the new ink and keeps its swing.
Five bars with their pieces: top, list, center, Marimba, strip.

A fixed piece can move along its bar and cannot be hidden.
Keys are grouped: panels, Marimba, places, settings.
Each key has Edit.

No key runs an owner act.
A routine is a prompt with purpose, variables, instructions and workflow.

A missed time is offered once when the dashboard opens, and never made up by itself.

A change is prepared as a diff.
Reasoning text is streamed and never saved.
Sections are marked fixed, yours, generated or part.

Generated sections cannot drift from code.
Steps are grouped as read, driver and owner.

Turning a step on never exceeds what the host allows.
The same steps with a description and the shape Marimba fills.
Names, Descriptions and Shape are three views of one list.
Each part says what it gives Marimba and which steps it brings.
Two parts have no switch.
A part turned off leaves the next turn.
Four zones: why, thinking, doing, keeping.
Runs fold into what they ran under, with a count on the mark.
What is not placed is listed.
A line exists only when a record names both ends.
The records behind the answer are lit and the rest are dimmed, not hidden.
The dock lists what was read.
An answer with nothing lit read nothing.
Counts first: decided, planned, gaps, waiting on you.
Each waiting item has its recommendation and Answer in Marimba.
The report puts words in the message box and presses nothing.
Sources are grouped by why, thinking, doing, keeping.
It says what leaves the laptop and to which model.
Adding a folder outside the project is an owner press.
A source is data. No instruction inside one is followed.
Rules, fences and limits are listed with their home file.
Nothing on the page has a switch.
Marimba may prepare a patch. Only the owner’s commit changes it.
Three rooms and a place for a new one, each with a small drawing, its counts and Enter.
Each room says what it left out.
Rooms share one set of records and store nothing.
Room 1 is the factory graph as the Canvas tab draws it today.
What is not on the map is listed.
Zoom out leads to the rooms.
Every plan and document, with its kind, state and what waits.
Filters by kind and by status.
The list is read from the plan registry, never kept by hand.
The whole plan opens inside the dashboard with its outline.
Each open questionable shows its options as buttons that put words in the message box.
The card shows how many answers would be applied and what would change.
Nothing is applied before the press.
Counts of sessions, asks, applied and not taken.
Each session opens to what was asked, decided, ran and touched.
It reads the sessions log and nothing else.
The request is quoted word for word with a link to its phase.
Six figures: outcome, calls, phase time, tokens, window share, candidate.
Every phase longer than one percent of the run draws to scale, and a shorter one draws as a point.
The overview bar shows the whole run at one scale.
The selected phase opens below with its tabs.
Four cards: model, prompt, context and tokens, tools.
What it says it did is the envelope, with its changed files.
Gates on its output list each check and its kind.
Route provenance shows requested, effective, observed and source for each field.
Where the time went is one bar split between commands and everything else.
A repeated command is named with its times.
The timeline shows recorded points and long calls on one clock.
The context line shows measured points and says it is drawn between them.
One line for each model turn, with its calls folded inside.
Filters: all, commands, changes, failed, long.
A failed call is marked and stays in place.
A template writes each line. No model is called.
Every record in source order with canonical times.
Filters by kind, a search, and the round.
Input comes first, and the result opens beside it.
A point has a diamond. A span has a duration.
Commands, checks, output, raw journal. No events tab.
The command table shows exit, time and the output file.
The check grid is commands by seven checks.
A host phase spends no calls, and the page says so.
The verdict is the largest word on the page.
Limits the reviewer named are listed beside the verdict.
The other provider is shown: built by, reviewed by.
What it saw lists request, files, results and the diff size against its cap.
The failed check, the path that tripped it and why no correction ran are in one place.
The phase strip is the prove workflow’s.
The engineer side holds what came in, and the owner side what goes out.
Each act before the first call shows its time and the reason given.
The journey’s checks, the closure record and the lifecycle are on the owner side.
The one act that remains carries the orange line.
Six tickets fit without a scroll: finished ones compact, the selected one keeps at least 40 percent.
A wait on the owner longer than a tenth of the run folds into one gap with its length.
Routes for each ticket show the tier list and what this run used.
The running ticket keeps the room, and queued work waits at the right.
The mark hangs from the line that says now, in Marimba’s own lane.
The live bar shows turn, calls, failures and the command running.
The bar always reaches now.
Four moments show compaction and focus.
Nothing reorders and nothing is hidden while the run moves.
A finished ticket compacts to 1 px a minute, at least 48 px, in 400 ms.
The running ticket keeps at least 40 percent of the track.
Four levels are tried in order: to scale, finished tickets compact, finished milestones fold, scroll.
The level that ends at each window width is in the table.
The milestone in progress never folds.
Lanes keep the icons of today.
A grid of items by route arm, with repetitions side by side.
Arms are compared by median time and verdicts, and tokens are marked as not comparable across providers.
A run that recorded a verdict shows its verdict first.
Prove never lands.
Documents is the first tab, with the three files and their sizes against their caps.
Open items are counted as settled, working choice and open, and become cards.
The documents live in session output and never in git until admitted.
Plan-admit lists its checks.
Three columns: team and rooms, the open room, cards.

A card gives what it blocks, the pick and why, options and Dismiss.
The owner’s grant for the task is shown with Revoke.
Every line is a journal record. The team writes documents and the owner commits.
Budget and rule text are never cards.
Grouping switches, then templates with a real line for each.
A number appears exactly as recorded, and a credential value is scrubbed before any line is written.
A model writing these lines stays off.
A phase kind decides its tabs, and the first tab opens.
The ten workflows and their phases are as listed.
Each record kind shows where the table says.
These notes explain the run screens, and nothing on this board is drawn in the product.
Each path visits its frames in this order.
An orange step is an owner press, and a dashed step happens outside any frame.
Two attempts of one change stand side by side, each with its own steps, state and mark.

An item set aside keeps its place and no longer turns the mark.
